newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end higher on world uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end higher on world uptrend.

text.p: Gold and silver opened higher on Wednesday in line with an uptrend in world prices and gained further by close on fresh wedding season demand, dealers said.

"Limited arrivals of imported gold and silver also helped prices recover, and speculators turned active buyers as the dollar gained against the Indian rupee," said a dealer. On Tuesday gold was down 15 rupees per 10 grammes while silver was steady.
A rising dollar and a world market recovery pushed the cost of imported metals upwards, the dealer said.
A revival in wedding season demand also helped market sentiment, dealers said.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes each) settled 200 rupees higher at 58,800 rupees per piece. They were down 200 rupees on Tuesday.
